title: Projekt 1034: Technische Umsetzung einer SBOM für KI (SBOM4AI)
description: Im Bereich der klassischen Software finden Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) – also Stücklisten, die Informationen über Softwarekomponenten und deren Abhängigkeiten beinhalten – schon lange Anwendung und werden vom Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) sogar gefordert. Diese Forderung gilt auch für KI-Systeme, jedoch ist die Idee einer SBOM spezifisch für KI-Systeme relativ neu. Erste Ansätze bergen daher die Gefahr, dass sie nicht alle notwendigen Aspekte im Hinblick auf die Transparenz der KI-Lieferkette abdecken. In diesem Projekt soll das im G7-Rahmen veröffentlichte Konzept "SBOM for AI - Minimum Elements" in die Praxis überführt und dafür eine technische Umsetzung der definierten Kriterien erarbeitet werden. Die SBOM für KI soll automatisiert erstellt und in einem geeigneten Format ausgegeben werden. Die erarbeitete Umsetzung soll anschließend allen Interessenträgern zur Verfügung gestellt werden, um so einen wichtigen Beitrag zur Cybersicherheit von KI-Systemen leisten zu können.

description: The Consulate of Canada to Germany, in Munich hereinafter referred to the “Consulate” requires routine cleaning services for its office building (the Chancery). Services must be provided in accordance with the specifications outlined in this Statement of Work and must support a clean, safe, and professional environment at all times while not interfering with the daily operations or activities of the Chancery’s occupants, clients, or visitors. The Consulate may also require very basic, unskilled services that would reasonably be within the capacity of a professional cleaner, such as shredding documents or watering plants. While the majority of the cleaning services will be performed at the Chancery on a daily basis, other cleaning services may be required on an as-and-when requested basis.

title: Analysis of the Beluga Fattening Cycle using photogrammetry
description: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) requires scientific expertise to assess the importance of spring in the annual fattening cycle of the endangered St. Lawrence Estuary beluga population. The work involves analyzing aerial drone imagery and morphometric data collected in 2024 and 2025 to evaluate seasonal changes in body condition among male, female, and pregnant belugas. The contractor will conduct advanced photogrammetric and morphometric analyses using image analysis software to refine sex identification, identify pregnant females, and assess changes in physical condition across age and sex classes. The work also includes the preparation and publication of two scientific articles that meet the standards of internationally recognized peer-reviewed scientific journals.

Ratkaisukokonaisuus otetaan käyttöön Hekassa ja Hekan tyttärellä Kiinteistö Oy Laivalahdentorilla. Tavoitteena on niin sanottu valmisohjelmisto-ratkaisu, joka kattaa Hekan tarpeet. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteillä. Hankinnan kohteena on selainkäyttöinen rekrytointijärjestelmä valmisratkaisuna ja ohjelmistopalveluna (SaaS) Salon kaupungille rekrytointiprosessin sekä sijaisvälityksen hallintaan ja koordinointiin. Valmisratkaisulla haetaan nopeasti käyttöönotettavaa ja jatkuvasti toimittajan puolesta kehittyvää ohjelmistopalvelua. Hankinta koostuu seuraavista pääkokonaisuuksista: • Rekrytointijärjestelmä • Sijaisrekrytointijärjestelmä • Käyttöönottoprojekti, ml. pääkäyttäjien koulutukset & testaussuunnitelma • Tuki- ja ylläpitopalvelut • Koulutuskannan käyttömahdollisuus • Integraatiomahdollisuudet Tavoitteena on saada kaupungille luotettava ja käyttäjäystävällinen rekrytointijärjestelmä. Järjestelmän tulee tarjota myös sijaisten hallintaan ja koordinointiin käyttäjäystävällinen ja mahdollisimman automatisoitu alusta. Tavoitteena on selkeä ja helppokäyttöinen työkalu koko organisaation käyttöön. Järjestelmän tulee olla ajantasainen ja uudistuva. Järjestelmään tulee sisältyä ohjelmantoimittajan tukipalvelut ja mahdollisten uusien ominaisuuksien perehdytykset käyttäjille. Lisäksi järjestelmässä tulee olla hyvät ja tehokkaat raportointi- ja analytiikkaominaisuudet. Sopimuskauden on tarkoitus alkaa helmikuusta 2028. Sopimus tehdään toistaiseksi voimassa olevana sopimuksena, jossa on kuuden kuukauden irtisanomisaika molemmin puolin. Hankinnan kohteen eli rekrytointijärjestelmän vaatimukset on kuvattu tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä.

description: Vantaan kaupunki pyytää tarjouksia ilmanpuhdistimien vuokraamisesta ja hankinnasta. Hankinnan kohteena ovat vuokrattavat ja ostettavat sisäilmanpuhdistuslaitteet julkisiin tiloihin, kuten koulu- ja päiväkotitiloihin, toimistoihin, arkistoihin, auditorioihin jne. Tilaajat hankkivat pääosin vuokrattavia laitteita, ja vähäisissä määrin laitteita tullaan ostamaan omaksi. Ilmanpuhdistimilla haetaan väliaikaista ratkaisua sisäilmaongelmien hallintaan käyttöä turvaavana toimenpiteenä. Ilmanpuhdistimien tulee olla tarkoitettu tähän käyttötarkoitukseen. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteellä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Kilpailutus suoritetaan avoimella menettelyllä, jonka perusteella jokaiseen osa-alueeseen puitetoimittajiksi valitaan kolme (3) vertailussa eniten pisteitä saanutta tarjoajaa etusijajärjestyksessä. Hankinta kilpailutetaan yhteishankintana niin, että Vantaan kaupunki julkaisee tarjouspyynnön. Kilpailutuksen perusteella tehdään samansisältöiset, sopimusluonnoksen (liite 1) mukaiset sopimukset Vantaan kaupungille, Kauniaisten kaupungille ja Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialueelle. Hankintayksiköt tekevät myös oman päätöksensä. Vantaan kaupungille tehtävien sopimusten perusteella hankintoja voivat tehdä Vantaan kaupungin kaikki toimialat sekä Vantaan Tilapalvelut Vantti Oy, VTK Kiinteistöt Oy- konserni, VAV Yhtymä Oy, VAV Asunnot Oy, VAV Palvelukodit Oy, VAV Hoiva-asunnot Oy, Hakopolun Liikekiinteistö Oy, Kiinteistö Oy Hakucenter, Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Maakotkantie 10, Pallastunturintien Liikekiinteistö Oy ja Asunto Oy Vantaan Katriinanrinne. Sopimustoimittaja voi tarjota samoin ehdoin tuotteitaan ja palvelujaan Vantaan kaupungin seuraaville konsernitoimijoille: Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy ja Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Sote-tilat. Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta, jonka jälkeen sopimusta voidaan jatkaa kahdella (2) yhden (1) vuoden optiolla (1+1). Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa ilmoitettuihin euromääräisiin arvoihin tai tiettyihin arvioituihin hankintamääriin sopimuskaudella.

title: Reintegration Services and Indigenous Community Support
description: An advanced contract award notice (ACAN) is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date and time stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 1. Definition of the requirement: Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement does not apply to this procurement. The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to provide in person support and assistance to Indigenous offenders to help them enter the workforce, including real-life, day to day mentorship and job preparedness development. The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objectives: The Contractor must provide reintegrative supports to Indigenous offenders, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit, such as Elder support, cultural teachings, counselling and hard and soft employability skills. The Contractor must provide jobsite support and engage with Indigenous offenders to check on morale, workmanship, and identify whether issues that may be arising that require intervention. 1.2 Tasks: The Contractor must provide reintegration and transition support services and interventions through job training including but not limited to: 1. Identifying and triaging, based on need and release dates, Indigenous offenders who require support for release planning. This includes but is not limited to, those who are under CSC custody with a release occurring during the period of the contract and are participating in CSC CORCAN and Pathways initiatives. 2. Providing continuous reintegration services to offenders under the Contractor’s care up to the offenders’ warrant expiry date (WED). 3. Providing in-person visits to Stony Mountain Institution’s minimum-security units as well as visits to the medium and maximum units according to an agreed schedule with CSC, to provide information and identify any Indigenous offenders who require support in the areas that the Contractor can provide. 4. Providing their training program to offenders. 5. Entering eligible offenders into the trainee pool for future employment. 6. Providing in class job training for offenders that demonstrate a need in that domain. 7. Providing job mentorship to offenders. 8. Providing in person support to offenders on the job site to check on morale, workmanship, and to identify issues requiring intervention by the Contractor support team. 9. Offering sweat lodges to offenders once every seven weeks. 10. Offering cultural teachings and engagement with staff through the Contractor’s Knowledge Keeper including lived experience and traditional teachings with the support of a Care Planner responsible for reintegration. 11. Providing on-demand counselling services through the Knowledge Keeper and Care Planner. 12. Offering wrap-around supports including, but not limited to case management, Elder support, cultural teaching, counselling, and skills that will assist them in the labour and trade field. 13. Offering wrap-around support through its training and support department including, but not limited to, housing support, healthy relationship teachings, money management. 14. Offering daily on-the-job check-ins through the Knowledge Keeper and On-Site Support to catch issues that may be arising that require effective, culturally appropriate interventions and reintegration support for First Nations, Métis, and Inuit offenders. 1.3 Expected results: Provision of in person support and assistance to Indigenous offenders to enter the workforce including, but not limited to, real-life day-to-day mentorship and job preparedness development. Provision of reintegrative supports including, but not limited to, Elder support, cultural teachings, counselling and hard and soft employability skills. 1.4 Deliverables: 1.4.1 For the delivery of reintegration support services to Indigenous offenders, the Contractor must collect information and prepare monthly reports in Microsoft Word or Excel and submit these reports by the 15th of the following month. These reports must include: 1. Services and support provided to Indigenous offenders both in institutions, healing lodges and on release in the community. 2. Services and support provided to CSC staff and other community partners. 3. A list of community supports and organizations to which Indigenous offenders were referred under the contract. 4. The Contractor must submit a year-end report by April 15th each year. It must submit all reports to Indigenous Initiatives, Regional Headquarters, Prairies via the following email: pra.rhqindigenousreintegration-reintegrationdesautochtonesar.pra@csc-scc.gc.ca. 1.4.2 Paper consumption: a. Should printed material be required, double sided printing in black and white format is the default unless otherwise specified by the Project Authority. b. The Contractor must ensure printed material is on paper with a minimum recycled content of 30% and/or certified as originating from a sustainably managed forest. c. The Contractor must recycle unneeded printed documents (in accordance with Security Requirements). 1.5 Constraints: 1.5.1 Location of work: a. The Contractor must perform the work at: 1. The Contractor’s place of business in Winnipeg, Manitoba 2. Eagle Women’s Lodge, Winnipeg, Manitoba 3. Stony Mountain Institution, Winnipeg, Manitoba 4. Jobsites in Winnipeg, Manitoba as identified by the Contractor in consultation with CSC 5. Institutions in Manitoba and within Winnipeg, Manitoba 1.5.2 Language of Work: The Contractor must perform all work in English. 1.5.3 Security Requirements: This contract includes the following security requirements: SECURITY REQUIREMENT FOR CANADIAN SUPPLIER: PWGSC FILE No. 21120-26-5393440 1. The Contractor must, at all times during the performance of the Contract, hold a valid Designated Organization Screening (DOS), issued by the Contract Security Program (CSP), Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC). 2. The Contractor personnel requiring access to sensitive site(s) must EACH hold a valid RELIABILITY STATUS, granted or approved by the CSP, PWGSC. 3. Subcontracts which contain security requirements are NOT to be awarded without the prior written permission of the CSP, PWGSC. 4. The Contractor must comply with the provisions of the: a) Security Requirements Check List and Supplemental Security and Classification Guide (if applicable), attached at Annex C. b) Contract Security Manual (Latest Edition). 2. Criteria for assessment of the statement of capabilities (minimum essential requirements): Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a statement of capabilities that it meets the following requirements: The Supplier must have 3 years of experience, within the last 5 years prior to the closing date of this ACAN, in providing a program that hires and trains Indigenous offenders for careers in the trades in Manitoba. The program must include preparation for reintegration from incarceration to release, to a job opportunity upon release. The Supplier must have 3 years of experience, within the last 5 years prior to the closing date of this ACAN, in providing a program to meet the needs of Indigenous offenders in the area of development of soft skills including, but not limited to, workplace culture, money management, parenting, healthy relationship training, cultural teachings and hard skills that include, but are not limited to safety certification and tool training. 3. title: Air Bath for Standard Resistors
description: An air bath for standard resistors is a temperature-controlled enclosure that maintains precision resistance standards at a stable and uniform temperature. Since the resistance value of standard resistors is temperature dependent, tight temperature control is essential for accurate resistance measurements used in thermometry applications such as standard platinum resistance thermometer calibrations. The laboratory is acquiring an air bath to replace the current oil bath system. Compared to oil baths, air baths provide cleaner operation, lower maintenance, no risk of oil contamination or leakage, and easier handling of resistors and wiring, while maintaining excellent temperature stability for precision measurements.

title: Geographic Information System Data Architect
description: This bid solicitation is being issued to satisfy the requirement of one (1) G.5 Geographic Information System Data Architect, Level 3 for Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada for Task-Based Informatics Professional Services (TBIPS) under the TBIPS Supply Arrangement (SA) method of supply. The primary objective is to establish a centralized geospatial data environment within the organization’s Azure-based Unified Data Platform (UDP). This environment will enable the efficient ingestion, validation, storage, integration, sharing, and spatial analysis of geospatial data across the organization, while supporting real-time relationships between spatial data and enterprise business datasets, automation, and more consistent, data-driven decision-making. In addition, the organization is looking for a cost-benefit analysis and recommendation of options to procure a modern geospatial platform, including how these options compare and integrate with HICC’s existing spatial capabilities and data ecosystems. The analysis will assess the potential value, costs, and implementation considerations associated with these platforms, and identify opportunities for location-based analysis, research, reporting, evaluation, automation, and application geoprocessing capabilities across the department.

description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) The Department of National Defence (DND), in support of the Canadian Forces Health Services (CFHS), has a requirement for the supply, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning, documentation, and warranty support of ten (10) Mobile Treatment Centre (MTC) cap-style slide-in modules. description: Kerry Education and Training Board (Kerry ETB), through Kerry College Monavalley Campus, invites tenders for the supply, refurbishment for training use, delivery and full installation of one (1) decommissioned wind turbine nacelle, complete with drivetrain and auxiliary systems, for use as a static training asset. The successful supplier shall be responsible for providing a complete, safe and fully installed equipment solution, including all labour, supervision, plant, lifting arrangements, fixings, accessories, connections, testing and handover necessary for the intended training use. title: Ireland – Design consultancy services – Request for Tender for the Provision of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content
description: The Commission is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified service provider for the design, management and delivery of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content. The successful Tenderer will be required to design, manage and deliver a structured programme of talent development and content development activities that strengthen professional capability within the audiovisual sector, facilitate collaboration between practitioners across the island of Ireland and support the development of high-quality audiovisual projects aligned with the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund. The services to be provided include, but are not limited to: • designing and delivering a structured programme of workshops, masterclasses, mentoring, networking events and audiovisual content development activities; • developing and implementing a fair, open and transparent recruitment and selection process for programme participants; • facilitating collaboration between audiovisual practitioners from across the island of Ireland, including participants from different jurisdictions, backgrounds and communities; • providing experienced facilitators, mentors and industry specialists to support participant learning and project development; • supporting participants in the development of audiovisual projects that demonstrate potential to progress to production and reflect the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund; • managing all aspects of programme delivery, stakeholder engagement, administration and communications; • monitoring programme delivery and performance against agreed milestones; and • providing progress reports, financial reporting and a final programme evaluation report in accordance with the requirements set out in Appendix 1 – Specification of Services.

title: Water Intake Facility at Radford Army Ammunition Plant
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice for informational purposes only to determine the interest and availability of potential qualified contractors for a new Water Intake Facility at the Radford Army Ammuntion Plant (RFAAP). RFAAP, located in Radford, VA is a Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) production facility providing state-of-the-art propellants, energetics, and munitions to support the Warfighter. All production at RFAAP depends on river water. Completing construction to the supporting infrastructure and in-water work will ensure the continued operation of the primary water intake at RFAAP and resilience of water supply to the facility.

title: Electricity Supply 2026
description: This is a COMBINED NOTICE/SOLICITATION for a commercial item prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation number, FA665626Q0022 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document includes incorporated provisions and clauses that are in effect through the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) and R-DFARS. This solicitation is full and open competition with the North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this commercial item is 221118 � Other Electric Power Generation; the small business size standard is 650 employees. UNIQUE REQUIREMENTS: Offerors (your company) must be registered with the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO). Only offerors registered with PUCO as electricity generation will be considered. Offerors shall be certified with company information is active and accurate in the System for Award Management (SAM). Reps and Certs must be complete in SAM. To be considered, ALL four (4) Unique Requirements must be met. ALL payments will be made through First Energy � Ohio Edison. Individual invoicing will not be considered. The electricity contract is for one (1) year and will be firm-fixed price with economic price adjustment � established price (FFP-EPA). All quotes must be stated in KWH unit price. *Supplies shall be domestic in origin. Suppliers must submit their quotes directly to the Government. Note: The Government will not sign supplier's terms and conditions agreements. ALL QUOTES MUST BE VALID FOR 15 DAYS. ELECTRIC GENERATION INFORMATION Transportation is through Ohio Edison - First Energy Annual consumption is estimated to be 9,275,000 KWH Account numbers for Ohio Edison are attached. Electric Power Usage for 12 Months Jan-25 813,899 Feb-25 748,067 Mar-25 709,431 Apr-25 642,192 May-25 686,427 Jun-25 705,251 Jul-25 921,309 Aug-25 867,636 Sep-25 784,071 Oct-25 667,175 Nov-25 654,875 Dec-25 767,671 8,968,004 The government's intent is to award a single contract between the government and the Contractor, to the lowest-price, technically acceptable offer. This notice does not obligate the government to award a contract, nor does it obligate the government to pay for any quotation preparation costs. Only written quotes will be accepted. Funding is not presently available. The following Revolutionary RFO Overhaul provisions and clauses are applicable to this acquisition and incorporated by reference. These provisions and clauses can be read in full text and accessed electronically at the following website: https://www.acquisition.gov/RFOoverhaul.

title: Minot Air Force Base Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) IDIQ
description: This is a Request for Proposal (RFP) for commercial, non-personal services prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 "Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services", Part 15 "Contracting by Negotiation", and Part 36 "Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts" procedures. This acquisition is 100% set aside for Small Business Concerns. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code associated with this requirement is 236220 "Commercial and Institutional Building Construction". The Small Business Size Standard associated with this NAICS is $45,000,000.00. The 5th Contracting Squadron, Minot Air Force Base (AFB), North Dakota, is requesting proposals to establish the base award(s) for a Minot AFB Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) vehicle. The MACC IDIQ will fulfill a continuous and recurring need for a broad range of design-bid-build and design-build construction projects to support the missions of the 5th Bomb Wing, 91st Missile Wing, and multiple tenant units assigned to Minot AFB. There is no seed project included with this solicitation. The MACC will have an initial five (5)-year ordering period with one (1), five (5)-year optional ordering period. The total aggregate maximum amount expendable under the entire MACC lifecycle SHALL NOT EXCEED $500,000,000.00. The guaranteed minimum amount over the life of the MACC is $500.00. The awardees' guaranteed minimum will be satisfied by attendance at the MACC Post-Award Conference. NOTICE TO OFFERORS (AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS): Funds are not available for the minimum guarantee. Award under this solicitation is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. The complete solicitation package is available in this posting. Anyone wishing to participate in this proposed procurement must obtain their copy from this website. Copies will not be distributed from the Contracting Office. All amendments will be posted on SAM.gov. Contractors are solely responsible for obtaining amendments from this site to update files. The complete solicitation package includes eight (8) attachments: 1. MACC Statement of Work 2. MACC Ordering Guide 3. MACC Specifications 4. Section L - Instructions to Offerors 5. Section M - Evaluation Factors for Award 6. Davis-Bacon Act Wage Determinations 7. Financial Responsibility Authorization Letter 8. Subcontractor Consent Letter NOTICE TO OFFERORS (MANDATORY SAM REGISTRATION): All prospective contractors must be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) at time of receipt of proposals. Failure to be active and registered in SAM will cause your firm to be ineligible for award. Offerors are highly encouraged to thoroughly review all solicitation documents prior to submitting their proposal. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by the agency. All contractors� questions in response to this solicitation must be emailed to 5CONS.PKA-C.MACC@us.af.mil no later than 31 August 2026 at 10:00 AM CDT. The Government will not be held responsible for answering any questions after this time. All questions/answers resulting from this solicitation will be posted to SAM.gov as an amendment.

title: Netherlands – Endangered species protection services – Opstellen Soortenmanagementplan (SMP) Gemeente Hulst
description: Het onderzoeksgebied bestaat in beginsel uit bebouwing binnen de komgrenzen van de gemeente Hulst. Naast reguliere woonbebouwing dienen bijzondere objecten binnen of direct grenzend aan deze komgrenzen expliciet te worden beschouwd, waarbij onderbouwd wordt welke objecten ecologisch relevant zijn en welke onderzoeksinspanning passend is. De opdracht omvat naar verwachting onder meer: • bureauonderzoek en gegevensinventarisatie; • gebiedsdekkende quickscan; • soortgericht ecologisch onderzoek en nulmeting; • analyse van beschermde gebouwbewonende soorten; • effectbepaling; • opstellen van een concept en definitief SMP; • mitigatie- en compensatiestrategie; • monitorings- en evaluatieplan; • proces-, administratie- en managementplan; • GIS-dataset, kaartlagen, metadata en dataoverdracht; • afstemming met overheden De opdrachtnemer is verantwoordelijk voor de samenhang tussen onderzoek, analyse, effectbepaling, planvorming, vergunningaanvraag, GIS-data, monitoring en overdracht Als voorbereiding op het veldwerk en het opstellen van het soortenmanagementplan wordt er een gebiedsbrede quickscan uitgevoerd. Op basis van de quickscan wordt vastgesteld of gebiedsuitbreiding noodzakelijk is en of er diersoorten worden toegevoegd aan het onderzoek. Uitbreiding van gebieden en soorten vindt plaats in overleg met gemeente Hulst. Onderzoeksgebied Het primaire onderzoeksgebied bestaat uit de bebouwde kommen binnen de gemeente Hulst, zoals voorlopig weergegeven op de door Gemeente Hulst aangeleverde conceptkaart “Komgrenzen gemeente Hulst”. Deze begrenzing is nog niet definitief en kan voorafgaand aan publicatie van de aanbesteding worden aangepast of nader worden gespecificeerd. Het buitengebied behoort niet tot de primaire scope, tenzij aanvullend onderzoek buiten de komgrenzen ecologisch of vergunningtechnisch noodzakelijk blijkt voor een vergunningwaardige onderbouwing van het SMP. Naast reguliere woonbebouwing dienen inschrijvers in hun onderzoeksstrategie expliciet rekening te houden met bijzondere objecten binnen of direct grenzend aan de voorlopige komgrenzen. Daarbij kan onder meer worden gedacht aan kerken, kapellen, monumenten, gemeentelijk vastgoed, maatschappelijk vastgoed, scholen, sportaccommodaties, zorgvastgoed, appartementencomplexen, hoogbouw, begraafplaatsgebouwen, molens, torens, oude nutsgebouwen en overige ecologisch relevante gebouwen. Deze bijzondere objecten worden niet op voorhand allemaal als volledig onderzoeksplichtig aangemerkt. Van de toekomstige opdrachtnemer wordt verwacht dat hij in de onderzoeksstrategie onderbouwt welke objecten ecologisch relevant zijn, welke onderzoeksinspanning daarbij passend is en hoe wordt voorkomen dat relevante verblijfplaatsen, kraamlocaties, massawinterverblijven, nestplaatsen of functionele leefgebieden buiten beeld blijven. De definitieve onderzoeksbegrenzing, objectcategorieën en eventuele objectenlijst worden vastgesteld in de aanbestedingsstukken. Gebouwbewonende beschermde soorten Minimaal worden er in het onderzoek de gebouwbewonenden vleermuizen, de gierzwaluw, de huismus, huiszwaluw en de steenmarter (mogelijk alleen als indicatiesoort) meegenomen. Op basis van de quickscan is eventuele uitbreiding mogelijk.

Computer-Aided Design (CAD): Providing 2D and 3D layout designs and Labor & Material (L&M) quotes. title: Biuro technikos nuomos paslaugų pirkimas
description: Atviras konkursas (supaprastintas). Pirkimo objektas – biuro technikos nuomos paslaugos (toliau – Paslaugos), t. y. spausdintuvų ir daugiafunkcinių spausdinimo-kopijavimo įrenginių (toliau – spausdinimo įranga) nuomos ir priežiūros, įskaitant, bet neapsiribojant, spausdinimo įrangos pateikimą ir paskirstymą į eksploatacijos vietas, pastatymą, sujungimą ir parengimą darbui, tvarkyklių pateikimą Perkančiajam subjektui ir jų atnaujinimą, spausdinimo, kopijavimo, skenavimo optimizavimo valdymo ir apskaitos programinė įrangą, jos diegimą ir konfigūravimą, autentifikavimo įrenginius ir jų montavimą, konfigūravimą, parengimą darbui ir priežiūrą, spausdinimo įrangos gedimų fiksavimą nuotoliniu būdu ir jų šalinimą, spausdinimo įrangos profilaktikos darbus ir laiku atliekamus spausdinimo įrangos besidėvinčių detalių keitimą pagal spausdinimo įrangos gamintojų rekomenduojamą periodiškumą, įskaitant tiekėjo specialistų darbo laiką, įskaitant visų spausdinimo įrangai reikiamų eksploatacinių medžiagų (dažomųjų miltelių, būgnų, nešiklių ir pan.) ir jų tiekimo į spausdinimo įrangos naudojimo vietas sąnaudas visą Paslaugų teikimo laikotarpį, Perkančiojo subjekto administratorių mokymus spausdinimo įrangos ir kitos techninės įrangos bei programinės įrangos naudojimo ir administravimo klausimais, Perkančiojo subjekto darbuotojų mokymus spausdinimo įrangos naudojimo klausimais. Paslaugos turės būti teikiamos Perkančiojo subjekto biuruose ir kitose patalpose Žolyno g. 15, Verkių g. 52, Justiniškių g. 14, Žolyno g. 22, ir Blindžių g. 12, Vilniuje ir nuotoliniu būdu. Pirkimo objektas į pirkimo objekto dalis neskaidomas. Pirkimo objektas, jo savybės, kiekiai (apimtys) ir reikalavimai pateikiami pirkimo sąlygų 1 priede „Techninė specifikacija“

description: Le présent marché a pour objet la réalisation de prestations de formation à la conduite en sécurité d’engins de chantier, de levage et de manutention, conduisant à la délivrance ou au renouvellement des certificats d'aptitude à la conduite en sécurité (CACES), au profit des agents de l’Etablissement public territorial du Grand Paris Seine Ouest. L'accord-cadre est conclu sans montant minimum ; avec un montant maximum annuel de 72 000 Euros HT Le marché est conclu pour une période initiale d'un (1) an à compter de sa date de notification. Il est reconductible tacitement trois (3) fois pour une durée d'un an à chaque reconduction, sans que sa durée totale ne puisse excéder quatre (4) ans.

title: Ireland – Radio, television, communication, telecommunication and related equipment – Containerised Communications Solutions
description: The Defence Forces have a requirement to procure a quantity of Containerised Communications solutions over the next 5 years. The purpose of these containers is to provide a mobile communications centre / office space which will be used to support Defence Forces operational deployments in the field. The containers will be mounted to an existing fleet of 4 x 4 trucks which will potentially change over time. To account for the changing nature of vehicle platforms the containers must be of a standard 20 Foot ISO (TEU) design complete with standard ISO corner casting / twist lock fitting to enable the rapid changing, mounting, demounting and movement via other means etc. When deployed the container must be capable to providing a shared work space for a minimum of 3 x communications operatives and capable of housing/running/sustaining a wide array of communications services in the field for up to 96 hours. The attached documents outlines the Mandatory Requirements (MR) and Optional Requirements (OR) for each of the individual Lots.

title: Corning and Holt 10 Levee Repairs
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District, is issuing a solicitation and awarding a single contract for construction services for levee repair at Corning and Holt 10 Levees, located in Holt County, Missouri. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) contract for this project. This will be a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. A site visit is scheduled for this project. The scope of work covered by this contract consist of furnishing all equipment, labor, operators, supervision / site superintendent, quality control, supplies, materials, and incidentals necessary to satisfactorily perform and provide construction to potentially include, but not limited to earthwork operations, bringing in fill and borrow material from a pre-determined site, haul road development, clearing of debris as necessary, erosion repair, rutting repair, levee surfacing, various stone surfacing/placement, installation of stone armored protection, installation and rehabilitation of drainage structures and associated apertures, and establishment of turf for repairs of compromised landside, riverside, and crown levee sections. A site visit is planned for this solicitation. The estimated magnitude of this construction project is between $250,000 and $500,000.

title: HogEye Cellular Camera Systems
description: Special Notice This is a notice of Intent to Sole Source. USDA APHIS, Wildlife Services (WS) intends to issue a Sole source award for the HogEye Cellular Camera Systems. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 334220 Product Service Code (PSC): 6710 Cameras, Motion Picture In accordance with the RFO FAR 12.201-1 (C)(2) Simplified procedures will be used for awarding the contract. The anticipated award date is September 28, 2026. (1) Mission Area and Contracting Activity. United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS), Wildlife Services (WS) located in Mississippi intends to award a sole source purchase order as it has been deemed that only one source is available to meet this specific requirement. (2) Nature and/or description of the action being approved. USDA APHIS proposes to enter a sole source purchase order with Wildlife Dominion Management, LLC. The Contractor shall furnish, deliver, and support a remote wildlife deterrent system composed of (a) live-video, cellular-enabled HogEye camera systems and (b) propane scare cannons, plus any integration hardware and software necessary to remotely trigger the cannons (and optional pyrotechnic launchers) from the camera interface. The suggested contractor is: Wildlife Dominion Management, LLC 1699 Moor High Rd. Crawford, MS 39743 UEI: YK2DFVBGDJN7 (3) A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency�s needs. Wildlife Dominion is the original manufacturer of the HogEye Cellular Camera Systems which is being requested. The company uses proprietary parts and software that are not made available to third-party service providers. As a result, no other vendors or technicians are authorized or technically capable of performing maintenance or repairs on this instrument, nor can they obtain the necessary parts to service or replace malfunctioning components. Because of these restrictions, only Wildlife Dominion can provide qualified technical support, authorized repairs, and genuine replacement parts for the HogEye Cellular Camera Systems. These instruments are crucial to the operational activities of Wildlife Services (WS). Improper maintenance or unauthorized repairs would risk equipment failure, work stoppages, and significant additional costs associated with restoring or replacing the instrument. (4) Identify the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition. The statutory authority supporting the placement of an order or establishment of a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) that exceeds the micro-purchase threshold on a sole source basis is: FAR 16.507-7 - Items Peculiar to One Manufacturer (5) Demonstrate that the proposed contractor's unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires using the authority cited. The Wildlife Dominion HOGEYE Cellular Camera Systems possesses unique capabilities not available in other commercially available camera systems. Wildlife Dominion�s integration of hardware/software allows for the remote trigging of propane cannons (and optional pyrotechnic launchers) from the camera interface. This feature is essential to the USDA�s ongoing, non-lethal harassment of piscivorous bird species to mitigate depredation to aquaculture facilities. No other manufacturer offers a spectrometer with identical calibration technology, analytical algorithms, or output compatibility. Competing instruments lack one or more of the following required capabilities: Solar-powered cellular camera system with infrared night vision and motion-triggered detection. Real-time alerts with image/video capture sent via cellular LTE network. Rugged, weatherproof design for field deployment in aquaculture environments. Integrated remote-control unit allowing linkage with deterrent devices (e.g., propane cannons, pyrotechnic launchers). Remote arming/disarming capability through secure app interface. Capable of sustained autonomous field operation without daily maintenance. Live video. Cellular-enabled camera systems. Propane scare cannons. Remote cannon detonation. (6) A determination by the Contracting Officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. The Contracting Officer has determined the anticipated cost to the Government of the supplies/services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable based on a thorough comparison of historical pricing data from the prior contract and the development of an Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE) using current market rates. (7) A description of the market research conducted, and the results or a statement of the reason Market Research was not conducted. Market research was conducted to verify the availability of comparable cellular camera systems from other vendors. The findings confirmed that no other cellular camera systems met our required compatibility and performance criteria. All responsible sources may submit a response which will be considered by the agency. Please email responses to Jeanine Goral Jeanine.J.Goral@usda.gov. no later than the response date of this notice. Telephonic inquiries will not be honored.

title: USPFO-PR Furniture Lifecycle Replacement
description: Update to Notice: This will requirement will be extended until 28 September 2026. Updated drawings/sketches will be provided through an official amendment. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Request for Quotations No: W912LR26QA044 Date of Solicitation: 09 September 2026 Contracting Office: USPFO for Puerto Rico � Purchasing & Contracting Division The Puerto Rico Army National Guard (PRARNG) has a requirement for the USPFO-PR Furniture Lifecycle Replacement. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12. The Government intends to issue a Request for Quotation for commercial products and incidental services to obtain modern commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) modular office furniture to replace obsolete systems across designated areas in Buildings 540 and 541 at Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico. The Contractor shall provide all logistics management, labor, tools, equipment, materials, and supervision necessary to perform: (1) systematic disassembly and on-site staging of legacy furniture; (2) procurement and delivery of new modular workstations, desks, credenzas, seating, and breakroom fixtures meeting ANSI/BIFMA and tropical climate durability standards; and (3) incidental installation, electrical connection of modular systems, alignment, and final site cleanup as defined in the Description of Requirements (DOR). This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. This acquisition is not subject to the Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS). This requirement is a 100% Small Business set-aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 337214 Office Furniture (except wood) Manufacturing. Quotations are solicited from Small Business Concerns. NAICS: 337214 � Office Furniture (except wood) Manufacturing Size Standard: 1,100 Employees PSC: 7110 � Office Furniture Estimated Award Date: 30 September 2026 Basis of Award: PRICE ONLY (see provision 52.212-2, SF 1449; quote conforming to solicitation requirements and DOR) Delivery Schedule / Period of Performance: 90 Calendar Days from date of award (8 to 12 weeks ARO) Place of Performance / Delivery Location: USPFO PR, Building 540 & Building 541, Borinqueneer Road, Fort Buchanan, Puerto Rico 00934-4069 Delivery and Acceptance FOB Point: DESTINATION Attachments Included: SF 1449 RFQ W912LR26QA044 DOR (Description of Requirements - USPFO Furniture Modernization) Pre-Proposal Site Visit A pre-proposal site visit will be held on 16 September 2026 at 10:00 AM Local Time (Puerto Rico) to inspect physical spaces across Buildings 540 and 541, verify dimensions, and assess layout/electrical connections. Attendees must coordinate base access and possess a valid driver's license. Attendance is not mandatory but highly encouraged. Fort Buchanan Base Access Requirements: Vendors planning to attend must submit the following attendee details in advance to coordinate base access clearance: Full Legal Name (First Name, Last Name) Full SSN Driver's License Number and State of Issuance Date of Birth Questions Submit questions, if any, no later than 15 September 2026 at 10:00 AM Local Time (Puerto Rico) to ng.prarng.purchasing-and-contracting.mbx@army.mil. Questions must relate to clarification of requirements, terms, and conditions only. The contracting office shall provide responses only to questions not specifically addressed in the solicitation document and attachments. Submission of Quotes All quotations need to be submitted no later than 18 September 2026 at 4:00 PM Atlantic Standard Time / local time Puerto Rico to NG.PRARNG.PURCHASING-AND-CONTRACTING.MBX@ARMY.MIL. Quotes received after closing of solicitation are late and shall not be considered. Submit signed and dated quotes to the office specified in this solicitation at or before the exact time specified. Quotes may be submitted on an SF 1449, letterhead stationery, or as otherwise specified. Offerors MUST include their Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code in their quote. As a minimum, quotes must show: (1) The solicitation number (W912LR26QA044). (2) The time specified in the solicitation for receipt of quotes. (3) The name, address, telephone number, and email of the quoter, and MUST include CAGE Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) registered in SAM.gov. (4) A technical description of the items and services being quoted in sufficient detail to evaluate compliance with the requirements in the solicitation and DOR. (5) Terms of standard commercial warranty (minimum 10-year structural, 3-year electrical). (6) Price and any prompt payment discount terms. (7) "Remit to" address, if different than mailing address. (8) Acknowledgment of Solicitation Amendments (if any). (9) If the quote is not submitted on the SF 1449, include a statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation. Quotes that fail to furnish required representations or information or reject terms and conditions may be excluded from consideration. (10) Quotes shall be submitted via electronic mail (email) to NG.PRARNG.PURCHASING-AND-CONTRACTING.MBX@ARMY.MIL no later than the date and time specified. Identify the email by using the SOLICITATION NUMBER in the SUBJECT LINE. Documents shall be sent in either PDF, Word Document, or Excel File. Do NOT submit quotes using web-based file sharing systems that require access, login, or external authentication. (11) Quotes received after closing of solicitation are late and shall not be considered. (12) Provide a completed SF 1449 and a copy of your vendor quote with pricing. Contact Information: Primary Point of Contact: Bernadette Barrios Rosario � ng.prarng.purchasing-and-contracting.mbx@army.mil | Tel: 787-289-1400 ext. 7696

title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. Disclosure of Magnitude of Construction (FAR 36.204 and DFARS 236.204) The acquisition will be procured as 100% Set-Aside for Small Business. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract. All responsible Quoters are encouraged to participate. The Request for Quotes (RFQ) will be issued on or about 19 August 2026, online through Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov; therefore, requests for hardcopies of the solicitation will not be honored. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code for this acquisition is 238170 - Siding Contractors. title: Ireland – Software package and information systems – UL1084 Enterprise-level Systematic Review Management Platform to the University of Limerick
description: University of Limerick is seeking to procure an enterprise-level, cloud-based Systematic Review Management Platform to support researchers, academics, students, librarians and research support staff in conducting high-quality evidence synthesis activities across the institution. The proposed solution must provide an integrated end-to-end workflow for systematic reviews and related evidence synthesis methodologies, including citation management, screening, full-text review, data extraction, risk of bias assessment, collaboration, reporting and publication-ready outputs. The platform should facilitate efficient collaboration between internal and external researchers, provide enterprise-grade administration and reporting capabilities, and support recognised methodologies such as systematic reviews, scoping reviews, rapid reviews, mixed-methods reviews and meta-analyses. The successful Tenderer will be required to deliver a fully managed Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, including implementation, training, ongoing support, systematic review methodological expertise, security and compliance assurances, and enterprise-level service management. The solution must align with the University's information governance, security, accessibility and architectural requirements, while providing value for money and supporting the University's strategic ambition to strengthen research excellence and evidence-informed decision-making across the institution.

title: RRSA 20V1163TB93L Diesel Engine Disassembly and Parts Harvesting
description: The U.S. Coast Guard has a one-time requirement for services associated with four MTU series 20V1163TB93L diesel engines currently stored at a Rolls-Royce Solutions America facility in Brownstown, Michigan. The requirement includes the following major tasks: Transport and complete disassembly of four MTU 20V1163TB93L diesel engines. Salvage of usable spare parts to support the National Security Cutter fleet. Salvage of all four crankshafts. Modification of two salvaged crankshafts to the current approved/improved radius design. Cleaning, preservation, packaging, and marking of salvaged components for long-term storage and future fleet use. Preservation, sealing, packaging, and shipment of two bare engine blocks for long-term strategic storage. Scrapping and disposal of two bare engine blocks. Inventory, sorting, preservation, and disposition of parts contained in Government-owned conex sea containers. Shipment of project deliverables FOB Destination to Government-designated locations. The engines identified for disassembly are: Engine Serial Number 5840363 Engine Serial Number 5840364 Engine Serial Number 5840397 Engine Serial Number 5840401 The salvaged parts will support sustainment of the U.S. Coast Guard National Security Cutter Main Propulsion Diesel Engines. SUBMISSION of INFORMATION: Interested parties having the capabilities necessary to meet or exceed the stated requirements are invited to provide information to contribute to this Sources Sought Notice including commercial market information and company information. Companies may respond to this Sources Sought Notice via e-mail, with subject line: SSN 70Z8526SRRSA_20V1163_EnginePartsHarvesting, to: Tatiana Sher at Tatiana.Sher1@uscg.mil and Kiya R Plummer-Dantzler at Kiya.R.Plummer-Dantzler@uscg.mil no later than the date identified within this notice with the following information/ documentation: 1. Name of Company, Address, and Unique Entity Identification Number (UEID) 2. Point of Contact, E-Mail Address, and Phone Number 3. Business Size and applicable to the NAICS Code 4. Capability statements shall include, at a minimum: Evidence of authority and capability to perform work on MTU 20V1163TB93L diesel engines. Evidence of access to required OEM technical data, procedures, tooling, engineering support, and approved modification documentation. Evidence of capability to disassemble, salvage, inspect, preserve, package, and ship MTU 20V1163TB93L engine components in accordance with OEM procedures and military packaging standards. Evidence of capability to perform or obtain approved crankshaft machining/modification to the current approved design.. Description of relevant prior experience with MTU 20V1163 series engines or substantially similar marine propulsion diesel engines. Description of quality control, traceability, chain-of-custody, inventory management, and preservation processes.
